title: Fleet headroom experiments — consolidated log
content:
Executive summary:
We ran a focused set of headroom/autoscale experiments across three regions (us-west1, eu-west1, ap-northeast1) to evaluate min/max pool sizing, cushion thresholds, and trigger heuristics for per-model and pooled GPUs. Goal: reduce idle GPU-hours while preserving 99th percentile latency SLO and reduce OOM fallbacks.

Experiment design:
- Period: 2025-10-20 -> 2025-11-02 (14 days, mixed traffic)
- Workloads: chat-small (short seq), chat-long (long seq), batch-embed (high QPS), rerank (spiky)
- Regions monitored separately; autoscaler configured per-region
- Variants tested (A/B windows):
  * Variant A (conservative): min=6, max=60, headroom=25% (buffer GPUs = 25% of running), scaleUpThreshold=70% util, scaleDownThreshold=45%, cooldown=3m
  * Variant B (aggressive): min=2, max=40, headroom=10%, scaleUpThreshold=80%, scaleDownThreshold=50%, cooldown=90s
  * Variant C (adaptive): min=3, max=50, headroom dynamic (10-30% tied to p95 latency), scale triggers include p95 latency slope + util crossing

Key metrics captured (per-region):
- Idle GPU-hours (sum of hours where GPU utilization < 10%)
- Provisioning lag (time between trigger and ready GPU capacity)
- p50/p95/p99 latency per model
- Fallbacks to lower-tier model or queued requests
- Cost delta (estimated $/day)

Top findings:
- Variant B saved ~28% idle GPU-hours vs Variant A but increased p95 latency violations in ap-northeast1 during predictable evening spikes (p95 up by 110–180ms vs baseline).
- Variant C matched cost savings of Variant B (~24%) while keeping p95 within SLO 95% of the time by using latency-slope to pre-warm. Adaptive headroom prevented the worst regressions.
- Min pool below 3 in eu-west1 led to frequent short-term OOM fallbacks for batch-embed; short rollbacks (scale-up after queue) added tail latency spikes.
- Cooldown length is critical: shorter cooldown (90s) reduces cost but makes the system oscillate for workloads with 3–7s burst patterns; hysteresis via successive-sample checks (2 samples required) reduced oscillation with minimal cost impact.
- Regional differences matter: us-west1 traffic shows smoother diurnal; aggressive settings worked well there. ap-northeast1 has higher variance; recommend conservative or adaptive.

Numbers (selected):
- us-west1: Variant A idle GPU-hours/day 42.3 -> Variant B 30.1 -> Variant C 31.2
- eu-west1: Variant A p95 latency 480ms -> Variant B 610ms (5% SLA miss) -> Variant C 490ms
- ap-northeast1: provisioning lag median 18s (A) -> 11s (B) -> 12s (C); but p99 latency spikes with B increased by 22%
- Cost estimate: Variant B ~$1,200/day for test fleet vs Variant A $1,600/day; net savings ~$400/day across the pool of 120 GPUs

Operational notes and anomalies:
- Observed autoscaler API rate limits in eu-west1 causing delayed scale actions during control-window (we hit provider 429s); mitigation: stagger control-plane actions and use backoff.
- A subset of models did not expose accurate queued-request counts; changed trigger predicate to use moving-average(inflight + queue) instead.
- Logging: we found mismatch between the autoscaler decision logs and the actual node-provision timestamps; tracking bug filed INFRA-2411

Recommendations (short term):
- Roll adaptive policy (Variant C) to eu-west1 and ap-northeast1 as experiment expansion for 2 weeks; keep us-west1 on Variant B for risk-tolerant workloads.
- Set min pool floor=3 for any region serving batch-embed until replication/queue sharding reduces per-node load.
- Use 2-sample confirmation for scale down triggers and require p95 slope check for scale up in adaptive path.
- Set cooldown to 90s for scale up, 5m for scale down to avoid oscillation.
- Add a small scheduled bump (pre-warm) 5–10 minutes before known traffic peaks in ap-northeast1.

Recommendations (longer term):
- Implement predictive preload using recent traffic autocorrelation (7–14m window) to pre-warm before spikes.
- Expose region-level config in the console with quick toggles for aggressive/adaptive/conservative.
- Improve autoscaler observability: include decision provenance (metric values that triggered action) and link to deployment events.

Next steps:
- Expand Variant C rollout to two more regions starting 2025-11-17 (owned by Anya Patel)
- Schedule infra-automation change for 2-sample hysteresis this sprint (INFRA-2420)
- Run a synthetic spike test for batch-embed (100% extra load for 5m) on 2025-11-21

Questions / open items:
- What cost threshold triggers reverting to conservative policy? Proposed: >1.2x SLO miss increase OR >20% cost increase relative to baseline.
- Is min pool floor of 3 acceptable for all customers? Needs product sign-off from Maya Chen.

Appendix and raw artifacts:
- Raw CSVs and charts in linked sheet (see linked_artifacts)
- Slack thread: #infra-autoscale (search: "headroom run Nov")
- Jira: INFRA-2334 (experiment plan), INFRA-2411 (logging mismatch), INFRA-2420 (hysteresis change)

Notes-to-self:
- Draft this into a short Confluence update if Variant C passes extended run.
- Check Dedicated customer telemetry: any customers on eu-west1 experienced user-facing degradations?
